note: PRE-REGISTERED from expected.md before any compiler was run. ONE defect, potentially TWO signatures. A hang report measured against a Debug ground truth is exactly the #3873 shape: there the Release build spun unboundedly while the Debug build asserted in ~2s on the same input, so a bare 'timeout' predicate scored Debug as no-repro and would have reported an open, always-reproducing bug as fixed. The disjunction exists so that either signature scores as a reproduction; which signature this defect actually has is a measurement, recorded in notes.md, not an assumption. Controls: the reporter names three necessary conditions and says removing any one avoids the hang, so control-no-member-fn.hlsl, control-no-buffer-access.hlsl and control-scalar-return.hlsl run with --expect no-match and   prove the predicate discriminates on exactly the axis the report names. || APPENDED AFTER MEASUREMENT (the sentences above are the pre-registration and are unaltered): both arms fired, on disjoint sets of compilers. timeout fired on all 20 stable releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607, every one of which is a Release build. internal_failure fired on main-debug, which exits 0xE0000001 in about a second with 'Internal compiler error: LLVM Assert'. They are one defect: the assert that fires is assert(0 && "Type mismatch.") at ScalarReplAggregatesHLSL.cpp:2662, reached from the guard 'if (!SrcTy->isStructTy())' at 2661, whose NDEBUG expansion leaves the bare 'return;' at 2663 that makes the caller's while (!V->use_empty()) loop at 2991 spin forever; the guard that would catch that, DXASSERT_LOCALVAR(... "Infinite loop while SROA'ing value, use isn't getting eliminated.") at 2994, is itself compiled out under NDEBUG. Had this been scored with a bare 'timeout' predicate, main-debug would have read no-repro and this open, always-reproducing bug would have been reported fixed. The three controls did NOT behave as predicted: only control-scalar-return.hlsl scored no-match, so the predicate is discriminating (it does return no-match on a near-neighbour input), but the axis it discriminates on is narrower than the report's three conditions. See notes.md.
